residual_limitation_ruling: Honestly stated and acceptable at this gate. The disclosed boundary -- 'the convention classifies FIELDS... It does NOT verify that a _now field's content is actually current -- only that its staleness is checkable rather than invisible' -- is precise about what kind of defect it closes and does not overreach into claiming more. This matches what was actually built: a naming schema plus a structural validator can guarantee every claim self-declares as frozen-or-live (making omission impossible, per the file's own citation of ADR-013's non-optional-argument and ADR-015's three-way-union reasoning -- the same 'inexpressible rather than discouraged' design principle applied to documentation), but no naming convention can verify that a live claim's CONTENT is true without a human or a separate fact-check rereading it against source. That second kind of error (a correctly-suffixed _now field that is nonetheless wrong) remains possible and is not claimed to be prevented. The distinction is exactly the one this whole four-iteration review has been drawing between arithmetic/structural consistency and judgment/content correctness (see the WSJF-inputs ruling from iteration 3, unchanged) -- and drawing it consistently, across a naming convention and a scoring convention, is itself evidence the project understands the boundary rather than asserting it once and moving on. Accepted without qualification.
